Declarations of Pecuniary Interest under the “Municipal Conflict of Interest Act”
notes:
Regional Chair K. Redman noted that January 25th marks the beginning of the Green Square Campaign that leads up to the National Day of Remembrance for the victims and survivors of the Quebec City Mosque attack. She also noted that January 27th is Holocaust Remembrance Day to remember the 6 million Jewish and 5 million non Jewish people that were killed during the Holocaust. 

There were no declarations of pecuniary interest .

items.title: Dan Driedger, Beyond Housing
notes: D. Driedger appeared before Council as the Executive Director of Beyond Housing and on behalf of a number of other housing organizations. He noted that the idea of housing over parking lots is an innovative idea and although there are a lot of unknowns, the idea should be studied. He encouraged Council to support the motion put forward by P. Wolf.

items.title: Dan Clements, Citizens for Cambridge
notes: D. Clements provided a presentation on behalf of Citizens for Cambridge in support of affordable housing over parking. A copy of the presentation is appended to the original minutes. He provided examples of existing housing over parking and stressed that the biggest challenge for affordable housing is finding locations. He noted that even if the savings on the land are eaten up by the costs of construction there are additional public benefits of infill development.

items.title: Brian Doucet, University of Waterloo
notes:
B. Doucet appeared before Council in support of housing over parking noting that the market is not addressing the problem of affordable housing. He highlighted that local governments are not able to build the housing that is needed but have the land that can be used. He stressed that selling land to developers does not allow for control over the affordability of housing but there are many options available if the housing built on public land. A copy of his written remarks are attached to the original minutes.

In response to a question from Council, B. Doucet encouraged the Region to look a small project that can be accomplished quickly.

items.title: Scott Hamilton, Cambridge
notes: S. Hamilton stressed that affordable housing is needed for people in all walks of life and is causing people to move out of Cambridge. He stated that density and intensification are needed to revitalize downtown cores and retaining ownership of the land allows municipalities to retain control. He encouraged the Region to support affordable housing over parking.

items.title: Kevin White, Kitchener
notes: K. White appeared before Council to express his concerns with Regional Council’s decision to not fully fund the Plan to End Chronic Homelessness. He highlighted ongoing issues with housing affordability in the Region and encouraged the Region to prioritize social services.

items.title: Erik Bodendorfer, Kitchener
notes: E. Bodendorfer appeared to express his concerns with Regional Council’s decision to reduce funding for the Plan to End Chronic Homelessness. He highlighted the decision to approve the Waterloo Region Police Services budget rather than fully fund social services and noted that more money spent on police does not translate into a safer community.

Planning and Works Committee Summary - January 16, 2024
Administration and Finance Committee Summary - January 16, 2024
Respiratory Season Update
notes:
Dr. Hsiu-Li Wang, Commissioner, Public Health & Paramedic Services/Medical Officer of Health, noted that Public Health is seeing moderate rates of Covid-19 and low rates of RSV and Influenza, that are consistent with provincial levels. She stressed that there continues to be an increase in Invasive Group A streptococcal disease in the Region and world wide. Dr. H. Wang noted that it can be life threatening and stressed the importance of seeking medical care, especially for high risk individuals.  

In response to a question from Council, Dr. H. Wang explained that the number of students that do not have up to date vaccination records is fairly typical. She highlighted the work that has been done in the last year to encourage parents to make sure that records are updated but noted that enforcement is required to achieve the level of vaccination rates that is need.

items.title: Other Matters Under Committee Of The Whole
CSD-HOU-24-002, The Plan to End Chronic Homelessness 2024 Budget Update
notes:
Peter Sweeney, Commissioner, Community Services, introduced the report noting that there is nothing new in the report since the plan was originally presented in November, except for the budget allocations. He highlighted that staff are recommending that Council either allocate the new investment of $10.2 million by an equal proportion relative to the original budget request, or prioritize fully funding the fee for service requests and reduce the remaining budget lines.

Responding to questions, P. Sweeney stated that there are many possibilities for reducing different line items, but stressed that all of the line items are needed in 2024 and staff are deliberately not recommending that Council prioritize one over another. He explained that staff are continuing to working with the YWCA in Cambridge to develop a viable proposal to be brought to Council.

In response to a question from Council, P. Sweeney noted that area municipal staff were involved throughout the development of the original report, but were not further consulted after Council’s budget decision.

motions.item_title: Planning and Works Committee Summary - January 16, 2024
motions.text: That the following recommendations from the Planning and Works Committee be approved: 1. That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following actions with respect to the proposed Grand River Transit (GRT) Hub at Conestoga College Doon Campus in the City of Kitchener as outlined in report EES-DCS-24-001, dated January 16, 2024: Approve the Recommended Design Concept for the Conestoga College Transit Hub as set out in Appendix A; and Increase the Consulting Services Agreement with Arcadis Professional Services (Canada) Inc. to provide engineering consulting for detailed design, contract administration, and site inspection services for the proposed Conestoga College Transit Hub in the City of Kitchener by $357,000 for a revised upset limit total of $590,100 plus applicable taxes, with construction contract administration and inspection to be paid on a time basis. 2. That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo: Enter into an agreement with Conestoga Students Incorporated and Conestoga College to implement a universal transit pass (U-Pass) program for an initial term ending August 31, 2027 with a mutual option to renew, in a form satisfactory to the Regional Solicitor, as described in Report TSD-TRS-24-002, dated January 16, 2024; Amend and extend the existing U-Pass agreements with the Wilfrid Laurier University Students Union (WLUSU) and Wilfrid Laurier University, the Wilfrid Laurier University Graduate Students Association (WLU GSA) and Wilfrid Laurier University, the Waterloo Undergraduate Students Association (WUSA), the University of Waterloo Graduate Students Association (UW GSA), and the English Language Institute at Renison University College (Renison ELI), for a term ending August 31, 2027 with a mutual option to renew, in a form satisfactory to the Regional Solicitor, as described in Report TSD-TRS-24-002, dated January 16, 2024; and Approve an interim U-Pass Fee Schedule and associated annual price increases for the 2025/2026 Academic Year and 2026/2027 Academic Year for all U-Pass programs, as described in Report TSD-TRS-24-002, dated January 16, 2024. 3. Whereas 6% of the current transit operating budget is allocated to Mobility Plus; and Whereas the current rate of undelivered trips on Mobility Plus is 5%, and has been as high as 15% historically; Therefore be it resolved that the target rate for undelivered trips will be 2.5% for 2024; and That staff continue to report quarterly on the rate of undelivered trips (previously called “unaccommodated trips”). 4. Whereas Mobility Plus’ total capacity is determined by resources (buses and operators), and the ability to optimize and group trips across the region; and Whereas staff are exploring an upgrade to the Mobility Plus booking and scheduling software; Therefore be it resolved that staff report back in-year, with the necessary operating and capital investments to accelerate the implementation of the Mobility Plus scheduling software upgrade and improve the optimization and grouping of trips.
motions.text_html:
That the following recommendations from the Planning and Works Committee be approved:

1. That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following actions with respect to the proposed Grand River Transit (GRT) Hub at Conestoga College Doon Campus in the City of Kitchener as outlined in report EES-DCS-24-001, dated January 16, 2024:

  1. Approve the Recommended Design Concept for the Conestoga College Transit Hub as set out in Appendix A; and
  2. Increase the Consulting Services Agreement with Arcadis Professional Services (Canada) Inc. to provide engineering consulting for detailed design, contract administration, and site inspection services for the proposed Conestoga College Transit Hub in the City of Kitchener by $357,000 for a revised upset limit total of $590,100 plus applicable taxes, with construction contract administration and inspection to be paid on a time basis.

2. That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo:

    1. Enter into an agreement with Conestoga Students Incorporated and Conestoga College to implement a universal transit pass (U-Pass) program for an initial term ending August 31, 2027 with a mutual option to renew, in a form satisfactory to the Regional Solicitor, as described in Report TSD-TRS-24-002, dated January 16, 2024;
    2. Amend and extend the existing U-Pass agreements with the Wilfrid Laurier University Students Union (WLUSU) and Wilfrid Laurier University, the Wilfrid Laurier University Graduate Students Association (WLU GSA) and Wilfrid Laurier University, the Waterloo Undergraduate Students Association (WUSA), the University of Waterloo Graduate Students Association (UW GSA), and the English Language Institute at Renison University College (Renison ELI), for a term ending August 31, 2027 with a mutual option to renew, in a form satisfactory to the Regional Solicitor, as described in Report TSD-TRS-24-002, dated January 16, 2024; and
    3. Approve an interim U-Pass Fee Schedule and associated annual price increases for the 2025/2026 Academic Year and 2026/2027 Academic Year for all U-Pass programs, as described in Report TSD-TRS-24-002, dated January 16, 2024.

3. Whereas 6% of the current transit operating budget is allocated to Mobility Plus; and

Whereas the current rate of undelivered trips on Mobility Plus is 5%, and has been as high as 15% historically;

Therefore be it resolved that the target rate for undelivered trips will be 2.5% for 2024; and

That staff continue to report quarterly on the rate of undelivered trips (previously called “unaccommodated trips”).

4. Whereas Mobility Plus’ total capacity is determined by resources (buses and operators), and the ability to optimize and group trips across the region; and

Whereas staff are exploring an upgrade to the Mobility Plus booking and scheduling software;

Therefore be it resolved that staff report back in-year, with the necessary operating and capital investments to accelerate the implementation of the Mobility Plus scheduling software upgrade and improve the optimization and grouping of trips.

motions.item_title: Councillor P. Wolf Notice of Motion
motions.text: Whereas the Region of Waterloo, like other regions across Ontario and Canada, is in the midst of an affordable housing crisis; And whereas, between 2021 and 2022, population growth in the region of Waterloo, grew at twice the rate of the Canadian average, with rental prices rising 141%, with 8,391 applicants on the waitlist for affordable housing, with an average wait time for housing at more than seven years; Now THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT Council request staff to include the following Regionally owned assets in scope as they develop plans to build more affordable housing in our community: parking lots, vacant properties, and buildings that could be re-purposed through redevelopment AND THAT staff provide council with a report that includes feasible locations, land and building ownership options, and construction concepts including potential partners.
motions.text_html:
Whereas the Region of Waterloo, like other regions across Ontario and Canada, is in the midst of an affordable housing crisis;

And whereas, between 2021 and 2022, population growth in the region of Waterloo, grew at twice the rate of the Canadian average, with rental prices rising 141%, with 8,391 applicants on the waitlist for affordable housing, with an average wait time for housing at more than seven years;

Now THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT Council request staff to include the following Regionally owned assets in scope as they develop plans to build more affordable housing in our community: parking lots, vacant properties, and buildings that could be re-purposed through redevelopment 

AND THAT staff provide council with a report that includes feasible locations, land and building ownership options, and construction concepts including potential partners.
